change_summary: Decider added three new surfaces publicizing eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json (Overview callout id=overview-eclipse-prereg, Part 4 §4.2 opening paragraph, Timestamp Error tab 3-command self-verification box); staged the JSON+.ots into docs/downloads/; corrected an earlier factual error citing Bitcoin block 947665 (which does not appear on the .ots attestation path) to the actual three blocks 947603/947604/947607 mined 2026-05-02 18:12:54/18:26:54/19:02:44 UTC. dispatcher-state artifact recommended priority=1 with head_item queue_id=568; adopted.
our_argument_summary: This change publishes the review's own eclipse-2026-08-12 pre-registration on three visible surfaces (Overview, Part 4 §4.2, Timestamp Error) with a three-command self-verification box, demonstrating the two-document OTS structure the Timestamp Error tab has been asking the dome author to implement since April. Corrects an earlier factual error (block 947665 → the actual 947603/947604/947607). The intent — practising what we preach and building an independently verifiable audit trail — is scientifically sound.

The pre-registration JSON pins the dome commit c3b9f56 (V51.1) as the source of dome-forced numbers via _meta.dome_repo_commit_sha and params_source_dome_sha, so the pinning is enforced.

independent_verification.ots_info_output: Three BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation lines: 947607 (via catallaxy), 947603 (via bob.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org), 947604 (via alice.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org). One still-pending PendingAttestation: finney.calendar.eternitywall.com. FOUR calendar servers total.

This proves the .ots file is a valid attestation against the actual Bitcoin blockchain.

holes_found.description: The Timestamp Error tab's 3-command self-verification box tells readers to run "ots verify predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json.ots" — but the modern opentimestamps-client CLI REQUIRES a local Bitcoin full node for this command. Empirical test on a fresh pip install of opentimestamps-client 0.7.2 (the exact package the review's install instruction names): "Could not connect to Bitcoin node: Cookie file unusable ([Errno 2] No such file or directory: '~/.bitcoin/.cookie') and rpcpassword not specified in the configuration file: '~/.bitcoin/bitcoin.conf'". A typical reader who copy-pastes the command will hit this cryptic error and may reasonably conclude the OTS proof is broken. This is the exact opposite of the review's intent ("no trust required"), and it undercuts the correction paragraph's credibility since the reader who tries to independently verify runs into a wall on step 2 of 3.
holes_found.recommendation: Change command 2 to one of: (a)  — this outputs each attestation's target Bitcoin block height and merkle root without requiring a Bitcoin node, and the emitted merkle roots can be manually cross-checked against a public explorer (fits naturally with step 3 of the box); OR (b)  — this parses the .ots file and prints block heights + calendar attestations without any network activity at all. Either variant works out-of-the-box for the target reader. Empirically preferred: option (a), because it emits the merkle roots explicitly and step 3 already tells readers to cross-check on mempool.space.

holes_found.description: The Overview callout and the Timestamp Error tab both state the .ots file was anchored "via three [separate/independent] calendar servers." A reader who runs "ots info predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json.ots" will see FOUR PendingAttestation entries (catallaxy, eternitywall, bob, alice) and only three BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation entries (947607, 947603, 947604). The eternitywall attestation is still pending as of 2026-07-05 re-verification. Our prose understates by omitting the fourth calendar. In a paragraph whose ENTIRE PURPOSE is to correct our previous OTS-related sloppiness (947665 → 947603/947604/947607), being loose about the calendar count opens the same class of unforced-error attack we're trying to close. A dome defender running the same ots info command sees a 4-vs-3 discrepancy in the very correction paragraph.
holes_found.recommendation: Rephrase both surfaces to: "attested via four independent calendar servers; three of those attestations have been confirmed on-chain (blocks 947603, 947604, 947607), and one (eternitywall) remains pending as of the latest re-verification." This is both accurate and reinforces the correction's spirit of exact self-representation. Part 4 §4.2's paragraph does not specify a calendar count and does not need to be changed.

holes_found.description: Overview callout: "OTS-anchored to Bitcoin blocks 947603 / 947604 / 947607 (mined roughly 10 hours later, about 102 days before the eclipse) via three separate calendar servers." The rounding "roughly 10 hours later" is accurate for 947603 (9.97h) and close for 947604 (10.20h) but understates 947607 at 10.80h. The Timestamp Error tab correctly uses "roughly 10–11 hours after stamping." Harmonizing the Overview to the more accurate range prevents a nit-picker from finding a numeric drift between two surfaces of the same claim.
holes_found.recommendation: Change Overview and Part 4 §4.2 paragraph phrasing from "roughly 10 hours later" to "roughly 10–11 hours later" (matches Timestamp Error tab). Small change, closes the drift.

holes_found.description: Overview callout: "a frozen control set of non-dome INTERMAGNET stations (MAB, DOU, WNG, SUA, BEL)." The JSON key labeling this set is candidate_non_dome_intermagnet_stations, described in the JSON as a "Pre-registered candidate set" of stations "within plausible NASA-predicted partial-coverage band" — i.e., these stations WILL experience partial eclipse coverage (>30% obscuration by selection criterion). In experimental-design terminology, they are a pre-registered candidate cross-check set, not a "control" set (control usually means untreated/unexposed). A precise reader clicking through to the JSON sees a naming inconsistency between the review prose and the anchored artifact.
holes_found.recommendation: Rephrase Overview to "a pre-registered candidate cross-check set of non-dome INTERMAGNET stations" or "a frozen 5-station cross-check set" — either matches the JSON's labeling. Same-word matching between prose surface and anchored JSON reduces attack surface.

stronger_arguments.description: The pre-registration file registers falsifies_our_analysis criteria — a symmetric commitment to revise our own verdict if specific conditions are met. This is the load-bearing scientific virtue distinguishing our review from the dome. The Overview callout and Part 4 §4.2 paragraph mention this in passing ("including the commitment detailed below in 4.2.6, under which we would revisit our own verdict") but do not make it the headline of the pre-registration. If we want the pre-registration to READ as the strongest possible response to the dome-author-timestamps-observations-not-predictions critique, the Overview should surface the bucket_3.falsifies_our_analysis criteria explicitly, not just refer down to §4.2.6.

The pre-registration JSON pins BOTH the review's own commit SHA (_meta.review_repo_commit_sha = cd8af4b5d9c4e0d182b71ba6734dd0f0310011b5) AND the dome commit SHA (c3b9f56). The review prose only mentions the dome commit. The review-side commit pin is arguably a stronger commitment because it prevents the reviewer (us) from retroactively editing our own analytical framework to match observations. Surfacing that we pinned both sides — us and them — strengthens the parity argument.

kernel_of_truth.description: This is a materially strong scientific move by the review team. Independent verification confirms every load-bearing factual claim in the corrected paragraph (docs/downloads/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:sha256=c2ba665057f4af8c65be52b0b7ee42a733e35b0445aa699d82ed328733a42660; docs/downloads/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json.ots:ots info→BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation(947603|947604|947607); mempool.space/api/block/... confirms block hashes + merkle roots + UTC timestamps 18:12:54/18:26:54/19:02:44 = 9.97/10.20/10.80h after 2026-05-02T08:15:00Z freeze). The pre-registration includes a bucket_3.falsifies_our_analysis clause (docs/downloads/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:bucket_3_falsification_criteria.falsifies_our_analysis) that commits us to revising our own verdict on specified observations — the symmetric-falsification standard the review has been arguing the dome author should adopt. Practising what we preach.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The core scientific move is intact and independently verifiable. The concerns above are execution-quality issues, not model-invalidating ones: (a) the 3-command box's ots verify command doesn't work for readers without a Bitcoin node (build-scripts/generate-html.js:2041), which is a MAJOR usability regression that undercuts the "no trust required" framing; (b) two of three surfaces say "three calendar servers" when the .ots file has four (docs/downloads/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json.ots:PendingAttestation×4 vs BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation×3), a self-inflicted precision hole in a paragraph whose whole point is precision. These are patchable in one small edit; the underlying pre-registration stands.

text_fingerprint.verdict: no verdict-change; content is additive to existing review

deeper_analysis: This queue item lands cleanly in the "decider-authored, HNOTE-driven content addition" bucket. The operator asked (via HNOTE-DECIDER-ECLIPSE-PREREG-PROMINENCE-2026-07-04T18Z) for the eclipse pre-registration to be surfaced on the review's public pages. The decider did that in three appropriately-scaled places (Overview callout, Part 4 §4.2 opening, Timestamp Error tab reference-example expansion) and — importantly — caught and corrected a prior factual error while implementing the change. The correction methodology is a small model of good scientific practice: run ots info, cross-check block explorer, publish the delta as a footnote with method, don't silently overwrite. From a dome-defender's perspective the strongest attack angles remaining are: (a) the sha256 verification command works but the ots verify command doesn't (usability regression that reads as sloppiness in the "physician heal thyself" surface); (b) "three calendar servers" appears in two surfaces but the .ots file has four (ots info readout available to any reader); (c) "control set" mismatches the JSON's "candidate set" naming. None of these compromise the load-bearing claim (that our review has published an independently-anchored prospective prediction for the 2026-08-12 eclipse 102 days ahead of the event). All are patchable in a single decider commit. The current_verdict_holds because the content addition is broadly correct; recommended_action is minor_edit because the four flagged issues are precise wording refinements, not structural rewrites.
